what-and-cadence.statement: Endpoint Data Scan provides visibility into sensitive data stored locally within all the endpoints connected to the organization's traffic. The report runs daily automatically, and considers a file sensitive if it contains at least one DLP engine or AI & ML category match.

quotes: Endpoint Data Scan provides visibility into sensitive data stored locally within all the endpoints connected to your organization's traffic.
The report runs daily automatically, and considers a file as sensitive if it contains at least one DLP engine or AI & ML category match.

report-sections.statement: The report opens in a new browser tab, and its Account section shows the username, organization name, organization ID and cloud name.

quotes: To access the Endpoint Data Scan Report, from the navigation menu, go to Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan; you're redirected to the Endpoint Data Scan pages in a new browser tab.
Click Account to view your username, organization name, organization ID, and cloud name.

report-page.statement: The Endpoint Data Scan page exports to PDF and shows Total Files Scanned as a count with accumulated size, and its top users can be exported to CSV. Top DLP Engines and Departments cover the last 14 days, and the trend graph shows no data if filters are applied.

quotes: Export the data into a PDF file.
Total Files Scanned: The total number of files scanned on the endpoints and their accumulated size.
Export: Export all the data in a CSV format.
Top DLP Engines: The graph shows the trend for sensitive files discovered for top DLP engines for the last 14 days.
Departments: This section shows sensitive files discovered for each department in a descending order within the last 14 days.
Sensitive Data Trend: The graph shows the trend for the sensitive files discovered
This graph does not show data if filters are applied.

range-distribution.statement: On the Sensitive File Range Distribution, the admin specifies the Medium range and the Low and High ranges are set automatically to match.

quotes: Click the Edit icon to specify the Medium range. The Low and High ranges are automatically set correspondingly.

per-user-drilldown.statement: For a specific user the report shows top DLP engines, AI & ML categories, file types and a 30-day activity trend, and admins can download a report with metadata for all the user's detected sensitive files.

quotes: including top DLP engines, AI & ML categories, file types, and a 30-day activity trend that highlights changes in the amount of sensitive data over time.
Admins can also download a report containing metadata for all detected sensitive files for that user.

user-investigation.statement: User Investigation shows each user's Incidents (user activities that triggered Endpoint DLP rules over the last one month), Activities (user actions that triggered DLP engines over the last one month) and Sensitive Files Discovered, which is updated every day. It filters by User, Department, Endpoint Name, Risk, Last Updated and Last Data Scan, and exports to CSV.

quotes: Incidents: The number of user activities that triggered Endpoint DLP rules over the last one month.
Activities: The number of user actions that triggered DLP engines over the last one month.
Sensitive Files Discovered: The total number of sensitive files discovered from all the user's endpoints. This data is updated every day.
You can add filters by clicking the plus icon. The available options are: User, Department, Endpoint Name, Risk, Last Updated, and Last Data Scan.
Export: Export the user-related data into a CSV file.

user-overview.statement: A user's Overview shows the Indicators of Intent rules the user triggered in the last 30 days, a section that is currently in Limited Availability. It also shows the user's total exfiltration attempts (allowed and blocked) and top destinations for the last 30 days.

quotes: Indicators of Intent: Shows a list of intent rules triggered by the user in the last 30 days.
This section is currently in Limited Availability.
Exfiltrated Data: Shows total exfiltration attempts by the user (allowed and blocked) for activities and incidents for the last 30 days and the split between the DLP engine and AI & ML category.
Top Destinations: Shows top destinations for activities, incidents, and intent performed by the user in the last 30 days.

user-data-at-rest.statement: A user's Data at Rest table shows the top 20 sensitive files based on DLP engines and AI & ML category match, with the dictionaries each file triggered; exporting the data gives the complete list of sensitive files discovered.

quotes: The table shows the top 20 sensitive files based on DLP engines and AL & ML category match. Export the data to analyze the complete list of sensitive files discovered.
Dictionaries: The list of DLP dictionaries triggered by the file.

user-timeline-event-types.statement: The user Timeline has Outbound events (created from DLP engine or AI & ML category matches on sensitive file exfiltration to Removable Storage, Printer, Network Share or Personal Cloud Storage, without any rule being triggered), Inbound events (sensitive files arriving from web, removable storage and network share on a DLP engine match, aggregated by source over a rolling 15 minutes), Incidents (Endpoint DLP or Device Control rules triggered) and Indicators of Intent.

quotes: Outbound: Events are created based on DLP engines or AI & ML categories, without any rule being triggered, when sensitive file exfiltrations are identified to the supported channels (i.e., Removable Storage, Printer, Network Share, Personal Cloud Storage).

Inbound: Events are created when sensitive files ingress to the endpoint from web, removable storage, and network share based on a DLP engine match. These events are aggregated based on the source with a rolling time of 15 minutes.
Incidents: Endpoint DLP or Device Control rules. When a rule is triggered, an incident is reported.
Indicators of Intent: Signals of risky user behavior on the endpoint, such as unusual data movement, policy bypass activity, security setting changes, or attempts to hide sensitive files.

user-timeline-details.statement: The user Timeline filters on Type, Channel, Destinations, Destination Type, Severity, DLP Engines, AI & ML Categories, Transaction ID and Rule Name. An event's date is the local time at the endpoint, and its Policy & Detection shows the triggered rule with the other rules that matched.

quotes: The available filter options are Type, Channel, Destinations, Destination Type, Severity, DLP Engines, AI & ML Categories, Transaction ID, and Rule Name.
Date: The date and local time at the endpoint location when the activity, incident, or intent was performed.
Policy & Detection: The triggered rule (the other rules that matched) with the actions.

device-investigation.statement: Device Investigation shows endpoint health, hovering over an unhealthy endpoint's error giving the reason, and a Nearby Sharing status. Allowed means Endpoint DLP enables nearby sharing but does not override or enforce it if another product blocks it, Blocked means Endpoint DLP prevents file transfers to nearby sharing devices, and Disabled means Endpoint DLP does not restrict nearby sharing. It exports to CSV.

quotes: Endpoint Health: Indicates the health of the endpoint. If the endpoint is unhealthy, you can hover over the error to view the reason.
Allowed: Endpoint DLP enables nearby sharing but does not override or enforce it if another product blocks the nearby sharing.
Blocked: Endpoint DLP prevents file transfers to nearby sharing devices.
Disabled: Endpoint DLP does not restrict nearby sharing.
Export: Click Export to download the Device Investigation details in a CSV format.

device-investigation-details.statement: Device Investigation filters on Endpoint DLP Version, Endpoint DLP Policy Version, Device Control Policy Version, Endpoint DLP Mode, Zscaler Client Connector Version and Anti Tampering Status. An endpoint's details show Sensitive Files Discovered from the last scan, performed every day, with a 30-day trend, and an Overview with the Endpoint DLP Installation Time and Device Control Policy Version.

quotes: You can add filters by clicking the plus icon. The available options are as follows: Endpoint DLP Version, Endpoint DLP Policy Version, Device Control Policy Version, Endpoint DLP Mode, Zscaler Client Connector Version, and Anti Tampering Status.
Sensitive Files Discovered: Shows the number of sensitive files discovered on the endpoint from the last scan. The scan is performed every day.
2. Overview
Number of sensitive files found: You can monitor the 30-day trend of sensitive data stored on each endpoint.
Endpoint DLP Installation Time
Device Control Policy Version
evidence.after: This tab shows general information about the endpoint, such as:

dlp-operational.statement: DLP Operational shows Total Endpoints (Windows and macOS devices on which Endpoint DLP is installed) and Users in Exemption Mode. The time frame that defines an endpoint's active status is Last 3 Days, Last 7 Days or Last 14 Days, and the report exports as CSV or PDF.

quotes: Total Endpoints: Indicates the total number of endpoint devices (Windows and macOS) on which Endpoint DLP is installed.
Users in Exemption Mode: Indicates the total number of users in exemption mode.
You can set the time frame to define the active status of the endpoint. The available options are Last 3 Days, Last 7 Days, or Last 14 Days.
Export: Click the Export icon to download the Endpoint DLP Operational Report in a CSV or PDF format.

dlp-operational-action-items.statement: DLP Operational action items include endpoints with anti-tampering disabled, a share of users in exemption mode above a threshold, endpoints offline for over two weeks, HDD scanning disabled, the Endpoint Data Scan report disabled, and macOS endpoints with Full Disk Access disabled. Full Disk Access being disabled prevents Endpoint DLP from functioning properly, and the page says to configure a Mobile Device Management (MDM) profile to enforce it.

quotes: Number of Endpoints On Which Anti-Tampering is Disabled <X>
Over <X>% of Users Are in Exemption Mode: A high number of users in exemption mode indicates misuse or potential abuse, resulting in security threats.
Number of Endpoints That Are Offline For Over Two Weeks - <X>
Scanning HDD Drives Is Disabled: Disabling HDD drives scanning might prevent visibility into sensitive data stored on these endpoints.
Endpoint Data Scan Report Is Disabled
Number of macOS Endpoints with Full Disk Access Disabled: Full Disk Access is disabled on macOS endpoints, which prevents Endpoint DLP from functioning properly and reduces protection coverage.
Configure a Mobile Device Management (MDM) profile to enforce Full Disk Access.

dlp-operational-policy-version.statement: An endpoint is considered to be using the latest version of the policy if both the Endpoint DLP policy version and the Device Control policy version are the latest, else it is considered to be using the earlier version.

quotes: An endpoint is considered to be using the latest version of the policy if both the Endpoint DLP policy version and Device Control policy versions are the latest, else it is considered to be using the earlier version.

end-user-report-viewing.statement: After the Endpoint Data Scan completes, the end user receives a notification with the number of sensitive files found locally. End users can open the latest report from the desktop context menu (Zscaler > Open Data Scan Report) and filter it by date, file type or file content; DLP engine details appear if configured by the admin.

quotes: After the Endpoint Data Scan is completed, the end user receives a notification with the number of sensitive files found locally.
End users can also access the latest report using the Context menu by right-clicking the desktop > Zscaler > Open Data Scan Report.
End users can filter the report based on date, file type, or file content.
DLP Engines: Displays the DLP engine details, if configured by the admin.

endpoint-dlp-mode-values.title: What the Endpoint DLP Mode values are
endpoint-dlp-mode-values.detail: Device Investigation filters on and shows Endpoint DLP Mode, but the captured articles do not define its values.

timeline-nss-mapping.title: How the timeline's Inbound, Outbound and Indicators of Intent events map to the NSS Endpoint DLP record
timeline-nss-mapping.detail: The timeline names Inbound and Outbound sensitive activities and Indicators of Intent events. The captured articles state no mapping to the NSS Endpoint DLP record type or to activitytype values.
